Open-source robots. First in your browser, then on your desk.

Try the SO-101 robot arm in a physics simulation and combat robots in the arena. Then you build the real robot: we tell you what to buy and where, and walk you through the build.

N° 02 — Try before you buysim.try()

From simulation to a robot on your desk. You can walk through every step in advance.

  1. sim.try()Simulation in your browser
  2. plan.parts()Parts buying plan
  3. build.arm()Build with the guide
  4. ai.connect()Connect your AI
  5. arena.fight()Combat arena
  1. 01sim.try()

    Try it

    Drag the blue ball and the arm follows. Click the cube and the arm picks it up by itself. Mouse or finger, with real physics.

    Start the simulation
  2. 02sim.learn()

    Learn

    Ten missions, from moving a cube to breakfast, a workshop and a lab. Record a motion and the arm repeats it, just like teaching a real SO-101 with LeRobot.

    Objects with physics
  3. 03plan.parts()

    Buy the parts

    You buy the parts directly from suppliers following our plan, with checked prices and a servo variant check. We’re preparing a ready-made kit – let us know.

    SO-101 kitParts buying plan
  4. 04build.arm()

    Build

    An exploded view from the original STLs shows every part. Walk through servo IDs, calibration and testing on a virtual arm before the box arrives.

    Servo setup dry run

Missions 06–10: real objects with physics

  • 59 scanned objects with mass and friction: food, dishes, tools, lab glassware.
  • Grab the arm by any link and pull; tap the jaws to open or close the gripper.
  • In the pen mission you draw with a finger or the mouse, helped by a top view.

N° 03 — Building the SO-101build.arm()

Seven stages, an estimated 10 to 19 hours of work.

estimate for a pair (leader + follower), parts printed yourself

  1. stage_0Before you buildTools, workspace and a servo check1–2 h
  2. stage_1PrintingPrinting the parts and removing supports1.5–3 h+ printer ≈ 16.5 h
  3. stage_2Servo IDsEvery servo gets its own ID, before assembly1–2 h
  4. stage_3MechanicsJoint by joint: base, shoulder, elbow, wrist, gripper4–8 h
  5. stage_4ElectronicsServo chain, driver board and power0.5–1 h
  6. stage_5First motionCalibration and teleoperation1–2 h
  7. stage_6Simulation and realityWhat you can try in the simulation today, and what you can’t0.5–1 hoptional

total10–19 h of work+ printer ≈ 16.5 h

N° 04 — Connect your AIai.connect()

Your Claude can drive the simulated arm.

Claude or another assistant with MCP support gets tools to control the simulated SO-101: joint moves, the gripper, a camera snapshot and missions. The arm moves in your browser tab, even when the tab is in the background.

  1. Add the server to Claude Code once:claude mcp add --transport http printedrobotics https://mcp.printedrobotics.cz/mcp
  2. Open the simulation and click Connect AI in the panel. A code appears.
  3. Give Claude the code and allow the connection in the tab.

Try telling Claude

  • “Pick up the cube and put it in the bowl.”
  • “Make the arm dance.”
  • “Solve mission 3.”
  • “Show me a picture from the top.”
Open the simulation → Simulation only: the AI cannot control a real arm. Our server only relays messages and stores nothing. Press STOP at any time.
N° 05 — Combat robotsarena.fight()

Robots up to 150 g. Fight your first match in the arena.

Physics with mass and friction, several maps, cameras including a TV broadcast view. Quick match, tournament, two players on one keyboard, or practice with no time limit.

  • In the garage you swap wheels, gearing and weapons; weight is kept under 150 g.
  • Project SVRN has a swappable front module: flipper, wedge or grabber. Opponents Kosa and Klepeto have their own original models.
  • After the match, replay a hit in slow motion and save the match as a file or a short clip.
  • A short guide walks you through the first match, and the Beginner opponent reacts more slowly. Motors, weapons and hits have their own sound.
Start the combat arena →
  • Pre-orderProject SVRNA 4×4 pusher with a flipper, wedge or grabber at the front.

N° 09 — How it workskit.flow()

Three steps between a GitHub repository and a robot on your desk.

  1. 01

    We print

    Parts from the project’s original STL files, in PLA+ or PETG, in your choice of colour. We check dimensions with calipers.

  2. 02

    We assemble

    Servos or motors, driver boards, screws, bearings, cables and power supply from the bill of materials — sorted by assembly step.

  3. 03

    We ship

    Within Czechia and the EU, with a printed guide and links to the project’s documentation and community.
